title: On Identification of Heat and Work in Quantum Many-Body Systems with Local Operations and Classical Communication
abstract: How we identify heat and work is a fundamental question in modern quantum thermodynamics. Usually, heat and work are attributed to changes in the density matrix and the Hamiltonian, respectively, during time-evolution processes in quantum systems. Recently, it has been recognized that this identification is ambiguous. Furthermore, quantum thermodynamics involving quantum measurement is still under development. Motivated by these on-going works, we consider a quantum many-body system from which we extract energy by local operations and classical communication (LOCC) according to the quantum energy teleportation (QET) protocol. The central idea to define heat and work unambiguously is based on a sharp insight into the optimization condition of LOCC. When LOCC is optimized, the extractable energy by QET becomes a daemonic ergotropy; thus, it can be attributed as work. On the other hand, when LOCC is not optimized, we have not squeezed out all the energy with the unitary operation. It means there is uncontrollable energy left in the system. The uncontrollable energy can be attributed as heat after careful treatment of many-body interactions. The heat term consists of nonlocal correlation due to communication between remote participants, and the correlation cannot be directly observed for the participant in the subsystem. Thus, this feature is consistent with the traditional perspective of heat as an uncontrollable energy. To deeply understand the nature of heat, we derive two types of generalized Clausius inequality in our effective quantum thermodynamics, and discuss the direction of the inequality. To justify our perspective, we examine a one-dimensional Kitaev-like model and discuss the physical meaning of effective temperature in our thermodynamics.
summary: This paper tackles the ambiguity in defining thermodynamic quantities like heat and work in complex quantum many-body systems. By analyzing energy extraction via Local Operations and Classical Communication, the authors propose that optimized extractable energy constitutes 'work,' while residual, uncontrollable energy defines 'heat.' They establish this framework using generalized Clausius inequalities tested on a Kitaev-like model.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental ambiguity in identifying heat ($\delta Q$) and work ($\delta W$) when analyzing energy extraction from quantum many-body systems.
main_result: Work is defined by optimizing Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) to extract daemonic ergotropy, while residual, uncontrollable energy defines heat, leading to generalized Clausius inequalities.
method: The authors analyze the optimization condition of LOCC using a Quantum Energy Teleportation (QET) protocol and derive two types of generalized Clausius inequalities for an effective quantum thermodynamics framework.
model_or_system: The study uses a general quantum many-body system Hamiltonian, specifically examining energy extraction via the QET protocol involving subsystems A and B. A one-dimensional Kitaev-like model is used to test the derived thermodynamic relations.
key_observables: Work ($\Delta E_B$), Heat ($Q$), Daemonic Ergotropy, Effective Temperature ($ eta_{	ext{eff}}$), and generalized Clausius inequalities (Type-I and Type-II).
important_parameters: The analysis depends on the optimization parameters of LOCC and coupling strengths within the Kitaev model.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that optimizing LOCC yields work, and the residual energy constitutes heat. The paper notes limitations regarding open quantum system descriptions (Lindblad equation) and the first law application.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the thermodynamic view of the model and QET protocol, showing how Bob operates locally based on Alice's measurement result.
paper_structure: The structure moves from identifying the ambiguity in heat/work definition to applying it within the QET framework. It then derives generalized Clausius inequalities, proposes specific definitions for $Q$ and $\Delta E_B$, and finally validates these definitions using a Kitaev-like model by checking consistency between bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, operational definition of heat and work in quantum systems that explicitly incorporates non-local correlations arising from communication (LOCC), which is crucial for understanding energy flow in realistic quantum devices.
